meta.title: Hivemind · Social swarm simulation
meta.description: Hivemind deploys a swarm of AI agents into a simulated internet built around your situation and reports how each group reacts.

home.heroTitle1: Build a fake internet around any event.
home.heroDesc: {brand} deploys a swarm of {agentScale} into a simulated internet built around your situation. It researches the topic, casts the people and organisations involved, and lets them post, argue and react. Then it tells you where they agree, where they split, and {optimalSolution}.
home.slogan: A simulated world for any event
home.systemReadyDesc: The engine is idle. Ask a question to start a run. Add evidence if you have it.
home.metricLowCostDesc: Simulated people per run, cast from the knowledge graph
home.metricHighAvailDesc: A Twitter-style feed and a Reddit-style forum, run side by side
home.step01Desc: Hivemind reads your evidence, or writes its own brief, and maps the people, organisations and relationships into a knowledge graph.
home.step02Desc: Everyone in the graph becomes an AI agent with a persona, a stance and a schedule.
home.step03Desc: The agents post, reply and react on two simulated social platforms, round by round.
home.step04Desc: A report agent interrogates the results and writes the forecast. A plain-language briefing covers the consensus and how each group would react.
home.step05Desc: Question the report agent or interview any simulated person.
home.promptPlaceholder: e.g. How will investors, regulators and the press react in the two weeks after the CEO resigns?
examples: How will customers, competitors and the press react if a major streaming service doubles its subscription price?
How will investors, regulators and employees react in the two weeks after a large bank announces 10,000 job cuts?
How will parents, teachers and tech companies react to a national ban on smartphones in schools?
home.pastePlaceholder: Paste an article, a memo, a press release or your own notes.
home.noEvidenceNote: Hivemind will write a background brief from what its AI model already knows about the topic. That can be out of date, so add documents for anything recent or private.
home.evidenceReady: Hivemind will build the run from your evidence.
home.publicNote: Runs on this site are public and appear in the history below, so do not paste anything private. Each run is capped at {rounds} rounds.
home.publicVisitorUsed: You've used today's free run on this site (one per visitor, and everyone on the same network counts as one visitor). Browse the earlier runs below, or come back tomorrow.
home.publicDayUsed: Today's {n} free runs on this site are used up. Browse the earlier runs below, or come back tomorrow.
home.publicBusy: Another simulation is running right now. This site runs one at a time, so Run opens again when it finishes (usually within 15 minutes).

step1.ontologyDesc: The model reads your documents and question, then designs the entity and relation types the graph will use.
step1.graphRagDesc: Documents are chunked and sent to Zep, which extracts entities and relationships into a temporal knowledge graph.
step1.buildCompleteDesc: The knowledge graph is built. Next, turn its entities into agents.

step2.simInstanceDesc: Create a simulation run and load the world parameters.
step2.generateAgentPersonaDesc: Turn the graph's entities into simulated people and organisations, each with a background, memories and a way of behaving.
step2.dualPlatformConfigDesc: The model sets the simulated clock, the feed algorithms, and each agent's active hours, posting rate and triggers.
step2.initialActivationDesc: Write the opening events and topics that set the simulated world in motion.
step2.setupCompleteDesc: The simulation is set up. Choose how many rounds to run.
step2.roundsConfigDesc: Hivemind plans {hours} simulated hours; each round covers {minutesPerRound} minutes.
step2.customTip: First run? Switch to Custom and use fewer rounds for a quicker, cheaper preview.
step2.publicRoundsDesc: This site plays the first {rounds} rounds, about {hours} simulated hours of the {planned} hours planned, so every run stays quick and cheap.
step2.publicRoundsNote: That covers the first wave of reaction. Run Hivemind on your own machine to play the full schedule.
step2.personaDimExperienceDesc: Complete behavioral trajectory in this event
step2.personaDimMemoryDesc: Memories formed from the seed documents

step3.oldSimCleared: Old simulation logs cleared, restarting simulation
step3.preparingGoBack: Preparing to return to Step 2, closing simulation...
step3.closeFailed: Failed to close simulation environment, attempting force stop...

step4.panelKeyFacts: Latest key facts from temporal memory

step5.reportAgentDesc: Ask follow-up questions. The report agent can search the knowledge graph, trace how stories spread and interview agents.
step5.toolInsightForgeDesc: Breaks a question into sub-questions and traces each answer back through the graph.
step5.toolPanoramaSearchDesc: Follows the graph outward to show how an event spread and who carried it.
step5.toolQuickSearchDesc: Fast lookup of facts and attributes in the knowledge graph.
step5.toolInterviewSubAgentDesc: Interviews simulated people in parallel and collects their views.
step5.chatEmptyReportAgent: Ask the report agent about any finding in the report.
step5.agentsOffline: These simulated people are offline. They can only be interviewed while their run is still up (on the public site, for about 20 minutes after it finishes). Ask the report agent instead: it can still search everything they said.
step5.chatEmptyAgent: Pick an agent and ask how they saw events unfold.
step5.surveyInputPlaceholder: Enter the question you want to ask all selected targets...
step5.selectAgentFirst: Please select a simulated individual first

graph.pendingContentHint: The run has finished. Agent memories may still be landing in the graph, so press Refresh in a minute to see them.
graph.waitingOntology: The graph appears here once the ontology is ready.

analytics.title: Analytics
analytics.empty: No agent actions logged yet. Start the simulation and this page fills in as it runs.
analytics.kpiApprovalHint: Support as a share of support + opposition
analytics.networkSubtitle: Who engaged with whom. Node size = engagement received. Arrows point at the author.
analytics.activitySubtitle: Every logged action, stacked by kind
analytics.postsSubtitle: Ranked by likes, reposts, quotes, comments and dislikes
analytics.selectHint: Click an agent in the network or the ranking to see who they influence.
analytics.noPosts: No post has been engaged with yet.
analytics.healthSubtitle: Whether this simulation is fit to forecast from
analytics.branchingSubtitle: How posts travel — and which agents never join in
analytics.branchingLow: Each post produces few follow-ons — threads mostly fizzle.
analytics.branchingMid: Some follow-on posts, but conversations still tend to die out.
analytics.branchingHigh: Posts keep spawning follow-ons — cascading is alive.
analytics.orphanShareHint: {count} of {roots} cascades never left the seed
analytics.cascadesSubtitle: Top cascades by size. Click one for lineage detail.
analytics.cascadesEmpty: No cascade trees yet — need a simulation DB with posts.
analytics.shapeOrphanHint: This post never branched. Nobody reposted, quoted or commented — an orphan cascade.
analytics.shapeBroadcastHint: Reactions fan out from the seed in one hop: a feed broadcast, not word-of-mouth.
analytics.shapeChainHint: The post moved through multiple hops — closer to a chain reaction than a single broadcast.
analytics.recapSubtitle: The story of this run in plain language, written from its posts and reactions.
analytics.recapWriteFailed: Couldn't write the full story, showing the quick summary instead. {error}
analytics.recapEmpty: Nothing has happened yet. The story starts once people begin posting and reacting.
analytics.recapArcLabel: Activity in each stretch of the run, split into posts, replies, approving and disapproving reactions
analytics.recapFoot: Quotes are real posts from this simulation. "Approving" means likes, reposts, quotes and follows versus dislikes and mutes. It shows how warmly posts were received, not what people think about the question. The forecast itself is in the prediction report.
analytics.briefSubtitle: What this run means: where the simulated voices agree, where they split, and how each group would react.
analytics.briefWriteFailed: Couldn't write the full briefing, showing the quick reading instead. {error}
analytics.briefEmpty: Nothing to read yet. The briefing fills in once people begin posting.
analytics.briefNoAgree: No point drew clear agreement across groups in this run.
analytics.briefNoSplit: No clear disagreement showed up in what people wrote or how they reacted.
analytics.briefGroupsSub: Groups come from the roles the simulation gave each participant.
analytics.briefReception: {pct} of {n} reactions to their posts approving
analytics.briefReceptionHint: How warmly this group's posts were received. It is not the group's opinion.
analytics.briefCompanies: How each company reacted, and its likely move
analytics.briefCompaniesSub: Companies and executives that wrote at least one post or reply in this run.
analytics.briefFoot: Every participant is simulated. "Likely next" and "Likely move" are inferences from what the simulated participants wrote, not statements by the real organisations. The PDF adds the story of the run and the run diagnostics.
analytics.castSubtitle: Every simulated participant, grouped by the role they play, with the people around the key actors branching off them. Click a name to follow them through the page.
analytics.castEmpty: The cast appears here as soon as agent setup starts.
analytics.castAria: Tree of {n} simulated participants grouped by role
analytics.castGrowing: Run in progress · more can join
analytics.castAdded: Added by Hivemind, not named in the evidence

godseye.title: Live situation from God's Eye View
godseye.hint: Fetch a live brief for a place (headlines, hazards, weather, air and sea traffic) and add it as a seed document.
godseye.placeholder: Place or coordinates, e.g. Taipei or 25.03, 121.56
godseye.notRunningHelp: Start it in your gods-eye-view folder with npm run dev, then check again. Hivemind looks for it at {url} (set GODSEYE_URL to change this).
godseye.scopeNote: Aggregate context only: cameras and tracking of individual aircraft or ships are excluded.
godseye.termsNote: Each source keeps its own terms, listed at the end of the brief. Google News headlines are for personal, non-commercial use only.
